# `tfctl profile set` reference

Set a profile configuration property.

## Usage

```shell-session
$ tfctl profile set PROPERTY VALUE
```

## Description

The `tfctl profile set` command sets the specified property in your active profile. A property governs the behavior of a specific aspect of the tfctl CLI. This could be setting the hostname and organization to target, or configuring the default level of logging across commands.

To view all currently set properties, run `tfctl profile display` or run `tfctl profile get` to get the value of an individual property.

To unset properties, use `tfctl profile unset`.

tfctl CLI comes with a default profile but supports multiple. To create multiple configurations, use `tfctl profile profiles create`, and `tfctl profile profiles activate` to switch between them.

## Arguments

- `PROPERTY` - (Required) Property to be set, such as `organization` and `hostname`.
- `VALUE` - (Required) Value to be set.

## Available Properties

The following properties can be set:

- `default_organization` - Default organization for commands
- `hostname` - HCP Terraform or Terraform Enterprise hostname (defaults to `app.terraform.io`)
- `telemetry` - Telemetry setting (`enabled`, `disabled`, or `log`)

Note: The `name` property cannot be changed using this command. Use `tfctl profile profiles rename` instead.

## Examples

### Set the default organization

```shell-session
$ tfctl profile set default_organization my-org
```

### Set a custom hostname

```shell-session
$ tfctl profile set hostname terraform.example.com
```

### Disable telemetry

```shell-session
$ tfctl profile set telemetry disabled
```

### Enable telemetry logging

```shell-session
$ tfctl profile set telemetry log
```

## Notes

- This command does not require authentication.
- When you change the `hostname` property, the `default_organization` and `token` settings are automatically cleared. You'll need to run `tfctl auth login` to authenticate with the new hostname.
- The hostname is automatically normalized (e.g., `https://` prefix is removed if present).
- Property values are validated before being saved.
- Changes take effect immediately for subsequent commands.
